description: Machine-readable expected outcome for every fixture in this directory. `verify-fixtures.mjs` reads this file and fails (non-zero exit) if any fixture's actual outcome does not match. `expected` is one of "accept" | "reject". For "reject" fixtures, `reason_code` must be present among the detected failure reasons -- for a named check this is a fixed string (e.g. "event_id_mismatch"); for a raw schema-validator error it is the JSON path the error occurred at (e.g. "$.relation"), following the same leading-token convention as agent-metrics/v1's fixture manifest.
notes: Design decision -- supersedes target absence is NOT a reject case: `cross-segment-supersedes` (accept) carries a well-formed supersedes_event_id that does not match any other event_id in this fixture set. This is intentional, not an oversight. trace/v1 is an append-only ledger that may be split across segments/files; a single-event validator has no way to know whether the superseded event lives in a segment it simply hasn't loaded yet. Rejecting on 'target not found here' would make partial-ledger validation (e.g. validating one day's new events) impossible. Referential integrity of supersedes_event_id, if ever checked, belongs to a whole-ledger compaction/audit tool, not to per-event validation -- this fixture set deliberately does not include a fixture that rejects for this reason.

fixtures.notes: Claude's binding_method (pre_assigned_session_id): the wrapper generates the UUID nonce and it IS the session_id, no separate join step. Payload carries binding_method for illustration only -- it is not part of the event_id identity.

Codex's binding_method (self_reported_thread_id): session_id is obtained after the fact from codex exec --json's thread.started event, not a pre-assigned nonce. Same relation (session_bound) as the Claude fixture, deliberately asymmetric payload -- this is the 'claude/codex 非対称' pair the spec calls for.
Exercises the identity exception: payload.window.{since,until} participates in event_id identity (re-importing the same window is idempotent) even though payload as a whole is excluded.
A plain artifact-edge relation (declares) with a two-part to_ref (logical_id + content_digest).

A correction: the second event declares a new revision of the same logical artifact (spec.md) and carries supersedes_event_id pointing at the first event's event_id. Both events individually valid, distinct event_ids, and the first row is never rewritten -- it remains in the fixture set unchanged.

See the top-level 'notes' entry above: supersedes_event_id references an event_id absent from this fixture set entirely, simulating a prior ledger segment this validator hasn't loaded. MUST be accepted at the single-event level.

event_id was computed, then to_ref.content_digest was mutated afterward -- the declared event_id no longer matches recomputing the identity hash over the actual body. A reader MUST recompute, never trust the declared value.
relation="does_not_exist" is not in the closed set. Rejected by schema enum validation.
occurred_at carries a +09:00 local offset instead of a literal Z suffix. This ledger has no concept of a local-offset timestamp; every writer MUST convert to UTC first.

A forbidden personal-dimension key ("reviewer") nested inside payload, which schema-wise is an unconstrained object -- so this is only caught by the dedicated personal-dimension scan, not by additionalProperties:false (payload has no additionalProperties restriction). This is exactly why the scan exists as an independent layer.
actor carries an unrecognized field. Rejected by additionalProperties:false on the actor object.

event_id uses the wrong version prefix (tr2_ instead of tr1_) -- a pattern violation distinct from invalid-event-id-mismatch's hash mismatch (that fixture has a well-formed tr1_ prefix and correct-looking hex, just the wrong hash).
